target_customer: Strategy consulting, life sciences advisory and investment banking firms
problem: Advisory firms spend analyst hours on decks, research and repetitive deliverables. Kenley turns firm processes into reusable AI agents and Office add-ins.
product_category: AI agents for consulting and advisory workflows

founders.name: Bolu Ben-Adeola
founders.background_notes: Education not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Noah Öhrner
education: BA in Computer Science, University of Cambridge

technical_complexity.rationale: Grounded document generation from firm knowledge plus Office add-ins and enterprise security is standard applied AI engineering with demanding enterprise requirements (the site cites SOC 2 Type II).

defensibility.rationale: Workflows tuned to a firm's templates create some lock-in, but general AI assistants and Office integrations compete.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No sourced evidence of any copying or acquisition; incumbent named from the product's Office add-in position, not from a source.

market_need_then: Consulting and banking work is document heavy. No quantified demand evidence was found.

branding.community_and_virality: A launch series called Advising the Advisors since May 2025 per a search summary; no community evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found; the name reads as a person's name.

outcome_analysis: Kenley is an active Summer 2024 company of six selling AI agents to consulting and advisory firms. The founders come from Bloomberg and Palantir and the site claims SOC 2 Type II, but no funding, named customers or exit were found, so the outcome is unknown.
notes: Funding search found no round; an Altss listing mentions family office investors with no amounts. The YC directory lists London while the site and one profile say San Francisco. The one-liner mentions financial services but the product pages focus on consulting. Competitor search returned only 2026 wealth management tools, so none listed.
